claims: A dispersal order is a lawful command issued by law enforcement requiring an unlawful assembly or crowd to break up and leave a specific area.
Dispersal orders are used when gatherings become riotous, violent, or pose an immediate threat to safety.
Failure to comply immediately after a warning can lead to arrest or the use of force.
Dispersal orders are used for riots, dangerous assemblies, or when conduct causes significant public distress or disorder.
Police are expected to give a clear warning indicating a safe route to exit.
Police are expected to allow reasonable time for people to leave before taking action.
Individuals who refuse to leave can be arrested for failing to disperse.
Police may use loudspeaker commands to clear an area.
Police may use mounted units to clear an area.
Police may use non-lethal agents to clear an area.
In some contexts, such as the UK, dispersal orders can be used to prevent anti-social behavior in specific areas for set periods.
